title: Licinius Mucianus
lead: The Roman governor of Syria from AD 67 (Wikipedia), a former consul, who first rivaled Vespasian and then pushed him toward the throne and led an army to Italy for him. Tacitus gives him a portrait (1:10, 2:5), and a long speech urging Vespasian to take power (2:76-77). Tacitus gives Syria four legions under him (1:10); Wikipedia's Vespasian page says he commanded three.
